 Brazoria County District Court
 Cause No. 2024-CV-0032
 Matthew Gregory, Plaintiff, v. Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance, Defendant
 Oral Deposition of Matthew Gregory
Date:
February 24, 2025
Location:
Offices of Paul & Kline Injury Lawyers
Examining attorney:
Richard Marshall, Ashford & Lyle LLP
Defending attorney:
Joseph Miller, Paul & Kline Injury Lawyers
Q: Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my full name on the record, if that's all right. You can use the case caption.
Q: That's fine for now. Where were you on the day of the collision?
A: I was driving home from work on a two-lane road in Katy, Texas. It was late afternoon and traffic was moderate.
Q: Tell me what happened.
A: A car came into my lane while going around a slow vehicle. I braked and steered to the right, but we still made contact nose to
nose. It wasn't a violent impact, but it was enough to jolt me forward and hit my knee on the dashboard.
Q: How fast do you believe you were traveling?
A: Probably around thirty or thirty-five miles an hour. I had just slowed for a turn.
Q: Did you get out of the vehicle at the scene?
A: I got out, but my knee was throbbing and I had trouble putting weight on it. An officer came and took a report. The other
driver was apologetic.
Q: When did you first seek medical care?
A: That same evening. I went to an urgent care clinic because the swelling got worse. They took X-rays and told me to follow up
with an orthopedic doctor.
Q: Describe the treatment you've received since then.
A: I've had physical therapy two or three times a week, and I was given a brace to wear when I walk for longer distances. I also
had an MRI, and the doctor talked to me about possibly needing further evaluation if the pain doesn't improve.
Q: How has the knee affected your daily life?
A: I used to run a few times a week and I haven't been able to do that since. Stairs are difficult, and I've had to change how I get
in and out of my car. I also had to ask my family to help with grocery shopping for a while because standing for long periods
makes the knee ache.
Q: Have you returned to your regular work duties?
A: I've returned, but I'm on modified duties. I sit more than I used to, and I take short breaks to stretch my leg.
Q: Before this collision, did you have any problems with that knee?
A: No. I had no significant knee problems before this. I was active and didn't have any restrictions.
Q: Is there anything else about the accident or your recovery you'd like to add?
A: Only that I'm hopeful the therapy will help, but I'm still dealing with pain most days.
</page>
